reasoning: The memcpy writes data->len bytes starting at bp, which sits at offset 3+padLen within the modulusLen-sized block (bp = block + 2 (0x00||BT) + padLen (pad) + 1 (after-pad octet)). Since padLen = modulusLen - data->len - 3, the write ends exactly at block+modulusLen, precisely filling the buffer with no overflow. The preceding guard 'if (padLen < RSA_BLOCK_MIN_PAD_LEN) return NULL' enforces modulusLen >= data->len + 3 + RSA_BLOCK_MIN_PAD_LEN, so the destination always has at least data->len bytes remaining. padLen is computed in unsigned arithmetic but assigned to a signed int; an over-large data->len produces a negative padLen that the guard rejects before any write. Therefore the memcpy is provably in-bounds.
